common_name: John Cabot Rose (Hardy Magenta-Pink Explorer Series Climber)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root roses in spring near a pillar, low fence, or trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; John Cabot was bred by Dr. Felicitas Svejda for Agriculture Canada and introduced in 1978 as part of the Explorer series developed for extreme Prairie winter hardiness.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun against a pillar, low fence, or trellis capable of supporting its vigorous, arching canes. John Cabot bears clustered, double, deep magenta-pink to cerise blooms with only a light fragrance, opening in a strong early flush with repeat bloom continuing into fall. Its Rosa kordesii-derived parentage gives it exceptional cold hardiness, surviving Prairie winters without the hilling or cane burial required by most climbers. Prune minimally, removing only dead or weak wood in spring, since the Explorer series was bred to need little winter protection or spray intervention.
sources: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada — Explorer Series Rose Introductions
